:::{#exr-normal-equations-vector}
#### Normal equations in vector notation

Define the matrix and vector

$$
A \eqdef \sumin \soprod{\vxi},
\qquad
\v{c} \eqdef \sumin \vxi y_i.
$$

Using @exr-rss-gradient-vector,
show that the [normal equations](#def-normal-equations)
can be written as $A \vcoef = \v{c}$.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#sol-normal-equations-vector}

Distribute the sum in the gradient from @exr-rss-gradient-vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\deriv{\vcoef} \text{RSS}(\vcoef)
&= -2 \sumin \vxi \paren{y_i - \dprod{\vxi}{\vcoef}}\\
&= -2 \sumin \paren{\vxi y_i - \vxi \paren{\dprod{\vxi}{\vcoef}}}
&& \text{(distribute $\vxi$)}\\
&= -2 \paren{\sumin \vxi y_i - \sumin \vxi \paren{\dprod{\vxi}{\vcoef}}}
&& \text{(sum of differences)}
\end{aligned}
$$

Each term of the second sum regroups as a matrix times $\vcoef$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\vxi \paren{\dprod{\vxi}{\vcoef}}
&= \vxi \paren{\tprod{\vxi}{\vcoef}}
&& \text{(dot product as a transpose product)}\\
&= \paren{\soprod{\vxi}} \vcoef
&& \text{(matrix multiplication is associative)}
\end{aligned}
$$

So the gradient is

$$
\begin{aligned}
\deriv{\vcoef} \text{RSS}(\vcoef)
&= -2 \paren{\v{c} - \sumin \vxi \paren{\dprod{\vxi}{\vcoef}}}
&& \text{(definition of $\v{c}$)}\\
&= -2 \paren{\v{c} - \sumin \paren{\soprod{\vxi}} \vcoef}
&& \text{(regroup each term)}\\
&= -2 \paren{\v{c} - \paren{\sumin \soprod{\vxi}} \vcoef}
&& \text{(factor $\vcoef$ out of the sum)}\\
&= -2 \paren{\v{c} - A \vcoef}
&& \text{(definition of $A$)}
\end{aligned}
$$

The normal equations set this gradient equal to $\vzero$.
Solving for $A \vcoef$ one operation at a time:

$$
\begin{aligned}
-2 \paren{\v{c} - A \vcoef} &= \vzero
&& \text{(normal equations)}\\
\v{c} - A \vcoef &= \vzero
&& \text{(divide both sides by $-2$)}\\
\v{c} &= A \vcoef
&& \text{(add $A \vcoef$ to both sides)}\\
A \vcoef &= \v{c}
&& \text{(swap the sides)}
\end{aligned}
$$

:::
